name: Combinatorics

papers.title: Multiplicativity of Vertex Energy Under the Kronecker Product
papers.abstract: We prove that vertex energy is multiplicative under the Kronecker product. Using this core property, we introduce a unified theorem to compute vertex energies for any graph operation obtained through the Kronecker product. As direct applications, we derive exact vertex energy formulas for semishadow, generalized splitting, and shadow-splitting graphs. Furthermore, we completely classify all blueprint matrices that preserve vertex energies.

papers.title: Constructions and Upper Bounds for Trifferent Codes
papers.abstract: A ternary code of blocklength $n$ is trifferent if every three distinct codewords have a coordinate at which they take all three values. Let $T(n)$ be the largest size of such a code. We prove that $T(n)=\Omega(1.162579^n)$ and $T(n)=O(n^{-1/2}(3/2)^n)$. The lower bound improves the exponential base $(9/5)^{1/4}=1.15829\ldots$ of K\"orner and Marton. It comes from a random system of overlapping local constraints, in which every position is read two or three times, followed by thinning and the deletion of nearby pairs and of the remaining triples that violate trifference. The required estimates reduce to finitely many inequalities, which we verify rigorously by computer. The upper bound improves our earlier bound $O(n^{-2/5}(3/2)^n)$.

papers.title: Graphs with the largest chainable index and their properties
papers.abstract: This paper provides a complete characterization of the set of graphs with the largest chainable index. In particular, it is shown that the number of arcs and vertex degrees of such graphs satisfy strong restrictions. Moreover, graphs with the largest chainable index form five parametric families, and exactly one of them consists of graphs that are not strongly connected. As a consequence, the number of graphs on $n$ vertices with the largest chainable index is computed, and the values of the primitive exponent for these graphs are calculated.

papers.title: Nash-Williams' Orientation Theorems for Infinite Graphs
papers.abstract: Nash-Williams proved in 1960 that every finite multigraph has a \emph{well-balanced} orientation: for all vertices $x$ and $y$, the maximum number of arc-disjoint directed paths from $x$ to $y$ is at least half, rounded down, of the maximum number of edge-disjoint $x$--$y$ paths. In particular every finite $2k$-edge-connected multigraph has a $k$-arc-connected orientation. He announced an extension to infinite graphs whose details, as far as is known, never appeared, and the two statements for infinite graphs have since been known as the strong and the weak orientation conjecture of Nash-Williams. We prove both, for multigraphs of arbitrary cardinality. For multigraphs with countably many edges we obtain more: a well-balanced orientation that is smooth (in-degree and out-degree differ by at most one at every vertex of finite degree) and, if the multigraph is $2$-edge-connected, has infinitely many arcs in each direction across every infinite cut. Such an orientation is obtained by K\H{o}nig's lemma from a sequence of finite orientation problems, each solved by the theorem of Kir\'aly and Szigeti on simultaneous well-balanced orientations. The infinite cuts are controlled by a canonical tree of $2$-edge-connected pieces with finite cores: once the cores are strongly connected and every finite cut is crossed in both directions, every arc lies on a directed cycle that uses only edges owned by one piece and edges of the cores of its children, and a counting argument of Thomassen does the rest. Neither local finiteness nor ends play any role.

papers.title: Graceful Colorings for Random Graphs
papers.abstract: Given a vertex coloring $c:V(G)\to [k]$, the graceful induced edge labeling is the induced edge coloring $c'(uv):=|c(u)-c(v)|$. A vertex coloring $c$ is a \textbf{graceful coloring} if $c$ is a proper vertex coloring and $c'$ is a proper edge coloring. The graceful coloring number $\chi_g(G)$ is the least $k$ such that there exists a graceful coloring $c:V(G)\to [k]$. We study the graceful coloring number for the Erd\H{o}s-Renyi random graph, $G_{n,p}$. In the diameter $2$ regime, we find the $\chi_g(G_{n,p})=n^{1+o(1)}$ using a connection between graceful colorings and Salem-Spenser sets. In the regime where $G_{n,p}$ is connected, but not diameter 2, we find that $\chi_g(G_{n,p})=\Theta\left(\frac{n^2p^2}{\log np}\right)$, using the forbidden submatching method and a connection between graceful coloring and the chromatic number of the square of $G_{n,p}$. Finally, in the regime where $G_{n,p}$ has constant average degree, we find that $\chi_g(G_{n,p})=\Delta(G_{n,p})+1$, by exploring the cycle structure of $G_{n,p}$.

papers.title: Inverses of split graphs via Ferrers diagrams and degree sequences
papers.abstract: A graph is a split graph if its vertex set can be partitioned into a clique and a stable set and is a partitioned split graph if the partition is also specified. The inverse of a partitioned split graph is formed by removing all edges within the clique and adding all edges between vertices in the stable set, while preserving the edges between the two parts. In this paper we compare two forms of the degree sequence of a graph: the conventional form and the block representation. We show the effect on the block representation of taking complements of graphs and inverses of split graphs, the latter of which is complicated by the fact that some split graphs have two different inverses. When there are two distinct inverses, we show how the degree sequences of these inverses are related to each other in both the conventional and block representations. We also demonstrate geometric interpretations of these results using Ferrers diagrams.

papers.title: Graphon hitting times: connectivity and minimum degree
papers.abstract: A classical result in random graphs states that the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph process becomes connected at exactly the moment its last isolated vertex disappears. The main goal of this paper is to establish a graphon analogue of this result. Let $G(n,W)$ be the inhomogeneous random graph sampled from a graphon $W$, and reveal its edges one by one in a uniformly random order. We prove that if $W$ is connected and the lower tail of its degree distribution satisfies $g_W(t)/t\to 0$ as $t\to 0$, which is needed for the connectivity of $G(n,W)$, then the connectivity and minimum-degree-one hitting times coincide asymptotically almost surely. We also determine when this hitting time occurs at scale $\Theta(n\log n)$, as in the binomial random graph model. Moreover, we give a simple analytic criterion for the transition to be localized in a $(1+o(1))$-multiplicative window, and construct graphons with minimum degrees arbitrarily close to zero whose transition is nevertheless sharp. Our approach uses Laplace transforms and vague convergence of rescaled graphon degree measures to provide a unified framework for analyzing low-degree vertices and connectivity transitions. Along the way, we revisit the minimum degree of~$G(n,W)$, giving simplified proofs of results of Hladk\'y and Viswanathan~\cite{HV} and establishing the limiting distribution of $\delta(G(n,W))$ under a second-order decorrelation condition.

papers.title: Helly complexes are minimal fillings
papers.abstract: We show that Helly complexes are universal minimal fillings. More precisely, if $X$ is a Helly complex, and $Y$ is a simplicial complex whose boundary is isomorphic to that of $X$ and such that the distances between the boundary vertices induced by $Y$ are at least as large as those induced by $X$, then $Y$ has at least as many vertices as $X$. The same type of inequalities hold for $i$-dimensional simplices of $X$ and $Y$ for all $i=0,1,\ldots$, i.e., for all coordinates of the $f$-vectors of $X$ and $Y$. When $Y$ is dismantlable, we show that the boundary isomorphism assumption can be weakened to a bijection between the vertex sets of both boundaries with an additional technical condition on boundary edges.

papers.title: Reflection subgroups and the Lookup Conjecture
papers.abstract: The Lookup Conjecture of Boe-Graham proposes a Bruhat graph criterion for rational smoothness of Schubert varieties in the flag variety $\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{B}$ of a complex reductive group. Its extension to Kac-Moody groups of affine type $\widetilde{A}_n$ was considered by Graham-Li. We prove the original conjecture as well as its extension to $\widetilde{A}_n$. Our method could be applied more generally to any Kac-Moody group after checking the rank-three reflection subgroups of its Weyl group. We also prove a parabolic version of the Lookup Conjecture for the type $A$ affine Grassmannian, where a stronger Bruhat graph degree monotonicity property in fact holds, and discuss the implication via the geometric Satake correspondence for weight multiplicities.

papers.title: Reflections in graphs
papers.abstract: We introduce and study an operation on graphs, called edge reflection, modeled on the effect of a reflection on the inversion graph of a permutation. The edge reflection length of a graph counts the fewest edge reflections needed to reduce it to the edgeless graph. Emptying a graph one edge at a time, or one vertex at a time, gives two upper bounds on this length, and each holds with equality precisely when the graph is a forest. For the edge bound we say more: the cyclomatic number of the graph bounds, above and below, the difference between the graph's size and its edge reflection length. Returning to permutations, we show that the edge reflection length of an inversion graph is at most the reflection length of any permutation realizing it, with equality whenever each connected component of the inversion graph has cyclomatic number at most one.

papers.title: Generalized oriented chromatic numbers and directed generalized coloring numbers of graphs
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $q$, we bound the $q$-transitive oriented chromatic number $\chi_o^q(G)$ in terms of the directed weak coloring number $\overrightarrow{wcol}_{2q}(G)$. For orientations with no directed cycle of length at most $2q$, we compare $q$-transitive oriented colorings with $\vec P_{2q}$-preserving oriented colorings. We also show that the directed strong coloring number at radius $2k-1$ bounds the density of every depth-$(k-1)$ shallow topological minor of $G$. These results characterize bounded expansion in terms of directed coloring numbers, oriented colorings, and homomorphisms of acyclic orientations.

papers.title: The maximum number of triangles in a graph without pentagons
papers.abstract: The generalized Tur\'an number $\ex(n,T,H)$ is the maximum number of $T$ in an $n$-vertex graph containing no $H$. Inspired by a conjecture of Erd\H{o}s on the function $\ex(n,C_5,K_3)$, Bollob\'as and Gy\H ori proposed the problem of $\ex(n,K_3,C_5)$. In this paper, we prove that $\ex(n,K_3,C_5)=(1/(3\sqrt3)+o(1))n^{3/2}$, finally solved this problem. As applications, we determine the asymptotic value of $\ex(n,\{\text{ind-}C_4,C_{5}\})$ which answers a question of Ergemlidze, Gy\H{o}ri and Methuku, and the asymptotic value of 3-uniform hypergraph without Berge short cycle which solve a conjecture of Gy\H{o}ri and Salia.

papers.title: Topological Clique Exclusion in Positively Curved Graphs
papers.abstract: We study locally finite graphs of positive Lin--Lu--Yau curvature and minimum degree at least $t-1$ under two exclusions: a topological $K_t$, denoted $TK_t$, and its locally topological version $TK^{(\leq2)}_t$, in which every replacement path has length at most two. The ordinary exclusion gives an $O(t^{7})$ maximum-degree bound by combining the classical density theorem for topological cliques with a curvature-driven rainbow-clique argument. For $K_t$-minor-free graphs, a Hall-matching refinement improves the maximum-degree bound to $O(t^3(\log t)^{3/2})$ and, for connected graphs, the order bound to $O(t^{19}(\log t)^9)$. For the weaker local exclusion, a codegree graph and Ramsey's theorem give the bound $\exp(O(t\log t))$. We also prove an exponential maximum-degree bound when the full 1-subdivision $K_t^{(2)}$ is forbidden as a subgraph, assuming minimum degree at least $t$.

papers.title: Low treebandwidth colorings, $p$-centred colorings and generalized coloring numbers
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $p$, let $\chi^{tb}_p(G)$ be the minimum number of colors in a vertex coloring such that every subgraph induced by $i$ color classes has treebandwidth at most $i-1$, for $1\le i\le p$. We establish quantitative relationships between these coloring parameters and generalized coloring numbers. If $\operatorname{wcol}_{2p}(G)\le m$, then $G$ admits a $p$-centred coloring with at most $[(p+1)m]^m$ colors; in particular, $\chi^{tb}_p(G)\le[(p+1)m]^m$. Conversely, if $\chi^{tb}_{k+1}(G)\le m$, then $\col_k(G) \le 1+4k^4\binom{m}{k+1}^{2}.$ Consequently, a graph class has bounded expansion if and only if its low treebandwidth coloring numbers are uniformly bounded for every fixed parameter. This gives a characterization of bounded expansion in terms of colorings defined by bounded ancestor distances in rooted forest layouts.

papers.title: A degree-stability method for the $p$-spectral Turán-type problem for disjoint color-critical graphs
papers.abstract: Let $F_1,\ldots,F_t$ be pairwise vertex-disjoint color-critical graphs with $\chi(F_i)=r+1$ for each $i\in[t]$. For $r\ge 2$ and sufficiently large $n$, Simonovits [Discrete Math. 7 (1974) 349--376] proved that the graph $K_{t-1}\vee T_{n-t+1,r}$ uniquely maximizes the number of edges among $n$-vertex graphs containing no copy of $\cup_{i=1}^tF_i$. In 2024, Lei and Li [Electron. J. Combin. 31 (2024), P1.25] established the corresponding result for the adjacency spectral radius. We prove that, for every fixed $p>1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, the same graph uniquely maximizes the $p$-spectral radius in this class. The proof reduces the problem to forbidding $t$ disjoint copies of a single color-critical graph and applies degree stability after deleting $t-1$ such copies.

papers.title: On canonical projections of the bipartite graph $D(k,q)$
papers.abstract: The bipartite graphs $D(k,q)$, constructed by Lazebnik et al. in 1995, are $q$-regular, edge-transitive, and of large girth. In this paper, we primarily instigate the canonical projections of $D(k,q)$. First, as a generalization of $D(k,q)$, we define a bipartite graph $\Gamma(\Omega,q)$, where $\Omega$, referred to as a rooted binary tree, is a finite subset of binary sequences closed under the deletion of any suffix. We then derive several significant properties regarding the symmetry, connectivity and girth of $\Gamma(\Omega,q)$. For arbitrary nonnegative integers $m$ and $n$, we fully characterize the connected components of $\Gamma(\Omega_{m,n},q)$, which is isomorphic to a canonical projection of $D(k,q)$ with $k\geq 2m+2$. Our results demonstrate that the connected components of $\{\Gamma(\Omega_{m,n},q)\}_{2\leq |m-n|\leq 3}$ form a novel family of graphs with large girth in the sense of Biggs.

papers.title: A general upper bound on broadcast function ${{B(n)}}$ using Knödel graph
papers.abstract: Broadcasting in a graph is the process of transmitting a message from one vertex, the originator, to all other vertices. We consider the classical model in which an informed vertex informs one of its uninformed neighbours during each time unit. A broadcast graph on ${n}$ vertices is a graph in which broadcasting can finish in ${\lceil \log_{2} n \rceil}$ time units from any originator. A minimum broadcast graph on ${n}$ vertices is a broadcast graph that has the least possible number of edges, ${B(n)}$, over all broadcast graphs on ${n}$ vertices. This paper presents a new general upper bound on ${B(n)}$ for all odd ${n}$ except when ${n=2^{k}-1}$ for an integer $k$. In order to achieve this bound, a vertex deletion method is applied to Kn\"odel graphs on ${n+1}$ vertices. To prove our result, we characterize all informed vertices in a Kn\"odel graph after every time unit by applying the standard and reverse dimensional broadcast scheme with any cyclic shifts from an arbitrary originator. Furthermore, we completely resolve the open problem about the existence of minimum average time broadcast graphs.

papers.title: Degree-respecting labellings with ordered neighbour sums
papers.abstract: In an exhaustive enumeration of hydrocarbons with only single bonds, carbon skeletons are generated as adjacency matrices and pruned by two rules: a vertex of larger degree receives a smaller label, and among vertices of equal degree, a vertex whose adjacency row is the larger binary integer receives a smaller label. The pruning is sound only if every skeleton admits a labelling obeying both rules. We prove that such a labelling exists for every finite simple graph, connected or not and with no bound on the degrees, and that the same holds when the weights $2^i$ of the labels $i$ are replaced by any strictly increasing real weights. The proof takes, among the labellings that order vertices by non-increasing degree, one minimising the sum over edges of the products of the endpoint weights.

papers.title: The hitting time index: bounds, a sharp threshold, the proof of a conjecture and the disproof of another conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove some new upper and lower bounds for the hitting time index ($HT$ index) of an $n$-vertex graph, showing along the way that the largest order of the index is $n^5$ and the smallest is $n^3$. More specifically, we prove the conjecture that the smallest value of the index is $\frac{n(n-1)^2}{2}$, which is attained by the complete graph. We also find a sharp threshold for the minimal degree $\delta$ so that the $HT$ index goes from an $n^4$ order to an $n^3$ order if the threshold is surpassed. We disprove the conjecture that the largest value of the index is attained by the $n$-path, and look at the lollipop graphs, some of which attain the $n^5$ order, and seem to be the natural candidates among which the largest value of the index should be attained.

papers.title: Cooperative colorings of cycles and uniform cycle factors
papers.abstract: A cooperative coloring of graphs on a common vertex set is a choice of one independent set in each graph such that their union covers the vertex set. We give a combinatorial proof that three cycles on a common vertex set always have a cooperative coloring. We also prove that, for every $\ell\geq4$ with $\ell\equiv1\pmod3$, there are three graphs on a common vertex set, each a disjoint union of cycles of length $\ell$, with no cooperative coloring. Together with known bounds, this determines, for every $\ell\geq3$, the least number $m$ such that every $m$ graphs on a common vertex set, each a disjoint union of cycles of length $\ell$, have a cooperative coloring. For $\ell\geq3$, this number is four when $\ell\equiv1\pmod3$ and three otherwise. These results answer two questions of Aharoni, Holzman, Howard, and Spr\"ussel.

papers.title: The $k$-disjoint paths problem for group-labelled graphs
papers.abstract: A $\Gamma$-labelled graph is an oriented graph with edge labels in a group $\Gamma$. Fix a finite abelian group $\Gamma$ and a positive integer $k$. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that finds $k$ vertex-disjoint paths joining prescribed pairs with a prescribed gain on each path, or determines that none exist. The result previously appeared only in the author's 2009 PhD thesis. This proof uses a reduction to unbreakable graphs and recent structure theorems for graphs drawn on a surface, and was found with the help of AI.

papers.title: Descartes' rule of signs for the topological degree
papers.abstract: We consider maps $F\colon\R^n_{>0}\to\R^n$ whose components are real polynomials, possibly with real exponents, with the same support of $N=n+k+1$ monomials, and we study the topological degree of $F$ on the positive orthant. In a previous paper we computed this topological degree in terms of signs of maximal minors, under a half-space condition which holds for generic exponents and coefficients. Here we use these formulas, together with their translation on the Gale dual side, to bound the topological degree. Our main result is a Descartes' rule of signs for the topological degree, which is as simple as the classical one: for two variables, the absolute value of the topological degree is at most half the number of cyclic sign changes, at the vertices of the Newton polygon, of the coefficients of any linear combination of the two equations, and similar statements hold in any dimension and on the Gale dual side. Our second result is a fewnomial bound: for generic exponents and coefficients, we get $|\deg F|<\frac12\min(M(n,N),M(k,N))$, where $M(d,N)$ is the maximal number of facets of a $d$-dimensional polytope with $N$ vertices, and this bound is sharp when $n=2$ or $k=2$. Our third result is a symmetry: using the H-duality of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsg\aa rd, we show that the set of possible values of the topological degree is the same for the parameters $(n,k)$ and $(k,n)$.

papers.title: List coloring degenerate graphs with requests
papers.abstract: We prove three results on the flexible list coloring of $d$-degenerate graphs. Following Dvo\v{r}\'{a}k, Norin and Postle [J. Graph Theory 2019], a graph $G$ is $(k,\epsilon)$-flexible if for any assignment $L$ of lists of size $k$ to its vertices and any choice of requested colors by a set $\widehat V$ of the vertices from their respective lists, there is an $L$-coloring satisfying at least $\epsilon|\widehat V|$ of the requests. The complete graph on $d+1$ vertices shows that if all $d$-degenerate graphs are $(k,\epsilon)$-flexible for some list size $k$ and satisfaction ratio $\epsilon$, then $k \geq d+1$ and $\epsilon\leq\tfrac1{d+1}$. Our results concern values at or near these extremes. For list size $d+2$, we improve the satisfaction ratio from an inverse exponential to an inverse polynomial function of $d$. For satisfaction ratio $\tfrac1{d+1}$, we prove that it is achievable for list size $2d$ as well as $\left\lfloor(d+2)\left(2-\tfrac1e\right)\right\rfloor$ (which is less than $2d$ for $d\geq 9$).

papers.title: Optimal bounds for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-constant-power error-correcting cooling codes
papers.abstract: High temperatures have dramatic negative effects on interconnect performance. In a bus, whenever a wire changes its state from ``0'' to ``1'' or from ``1'' to ``0'', Joule heating causes the temperature to rise. Constant-power error-correcting cooling (CPECC) codes, introduced in [IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, 66 (2020), 4804--4818], are coding schemes that can simultaneously control the peak temperature and the average power consumption of on-chip buses while providing error-correction capability for transmitted information. This paper establishes a new upper bound for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-CPECC codes for $t<w-3$ by some graph-theoretic techniques and the probabilistic method, and constructs several new families of optimal CPECC codes using the asymptotic existence result for GDDs. For $t\geq w-3$, this paper also provides a new upper bound for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-CPECC codes by some hypergraph-theoretic techniques, and several new families of CPECC codes attaining the resulting upper bounds using RBIBDs. The previous upper bound for $(n,t,w,w-2)$-CPECC codes in [arXiv:2608.08742] is a special case of our upper bound.

papers.title: Counting Classical Fullerenes I: Exact Enumeration and Generic Achiral Symmetry
papers.abstract: We give an exact arithmetic formula for the number of classical fullerenes on $2m$ vertices. The oriented count is known; the new contribution counts achiral fullerenes, those admitting an orientation-reversing symmetry. We transport these symmetries to a lattice, classify eleven types, and express their contribution as seven weighted orbit counts. The complete formula is printed here, together with an exact algorithm producing all counts through index $M$ in quasilinear bit time with fast integer multiplication. We also prove that the proportion of achiral fullerenes with a unique orientation-reversing symmetry tends to one as the size increases. That symmetry is either a reflection or a fixed-point-free involution, with cumulative proportions $527/529$ and $2/529$. Among all fullerenes on $2m$ vertices, the achiral proportion has order $m^{-5}$; the same order holds cumulatively. The exceptional achiral classes with nontrivial orientation-preserving symmetry number $O(m^2)$.

papers.title: Counting Classical Fullerenes VII: Arithmetic Unranking of Fullerene Isomers
papers.abstract: Given a vertex number $2m$ and a rank, we construct the corresponding ordinary fullerene as a planar adjacency list. Choosing the rank uniformly therefore samples ordinary isomorphism classes exactly from the vertex number alone. We select an integral period by counting lattice points on a quadratic level in polytopes with fixed facet directions. For a fixed positive semidefinite integral form on a box of radius $H$, with a linear term of coefficients $O(H)$, the algorithm computes all level counts simultaneously in $O(H^2\operatorname{polylog}(2m))$ bit operations when $H=O(\sqrt m)$ and the facet offsets have $O(\log(2m))$ bits. A signed decomposition into orthogonal simplices gives this bound. For fullerenes we use deterministic $O(m^2\operatorname{polylog}(2m))$ bit work to construct an index of $O(m\log(2m))$ bits. With this index a rank costs $O(m\operatorname{polylog}(2m))$ bit work, uniformly in the rank. Two families of recuts let energy descent escape self-contacts in the slit polygon. The decoder then writes the graph from its selected period in $O(m)$ arithmetic word operations.

papers.title: Hall's condition between adjacent levels of the face lattice of the permutohedron
papers.abstract: Let $\OP$ be the poset of ordered set partitions of $[n]$, ordered by merging adjacent blocks; with a bottom element adjoined it is the face lattice of the permutohedron. Whether it has the Sperner property is open. We show that for every pair of adjacent levels, the smaller one can be matched into the larger one by parent--child pairs, except possibly for the pairs $(j,j+1)$ with $(28n-36)/39<j<(13n+5)/18$ (for small $n$ the window is slightly smaller still). This window has width about $n/234\approx0.0043\,n$. The largest level lies near $n/(2\ln2)\approx0.7213\,n$, which we prove using the law of the block sizes of a uniformly random ordered set partition of $[n]$, and for $n$ large it falls inside the window. Since the level sizes are log-concave, Hall's condition for all pairs would make $\OP$ Sperner. The proofs use explicit weights on the parent--child pairs; they reduce to a finite inequality between pairs of adjacent blocks. We explain why the simplest weights fail exactly at the boundary of a much larger window, and report computations supporting Hall's condition inside the window: exactly for $n\le14$, and by equalizing flows for every window pair with $n\le25$.

papers.title: Induced Independence Levels and Signed Enumeration in Powers of Cycles
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$ we study the distribution of the independence numbers $\alpha(G[S])$ over its vertex-induced subgraphs, together with signed Boolean-lattice sums over fixed independence-number levels. For the $r$th power $C_n^r$ of a cycle, we establish, in the range $n\ge 2rk+r+1$, a unique representation of each subset $S$ with $\alpha(C_n^r[S])=k$ by an independent $k$-set and its forward neighborhood. The resulting Boolean-interval partition gives exact enumeration by subset cardinality. We also prove reconstruction of partially deleted forward neighborhoods and determine the support, signs, and multiplicities of the corresponding upper M\"obius transform. For cycle squares we develop a complementary greedy-chain method for signed enumeration, with a five-transition classification and explicit staircase and two-gap cancellation identities.

papers.title: Symplectic bumpless pipe dreams
papers.abstract: Bumpless pipe dreams are combinatorial objects in bijection with alternating sign matrices. Double Grothendieck polynomials can be expressed as weighted sums over bumpless pipe dreams, a perspective that has led to many advances in the combinatorics of Schubert calculus and connections with integrable systems. We introduce symplectic bumpless pipe dreams and present an analogous formula for symplectic Grothendieck polynomials, which represent the equivariant K-theoretic classes of Sp(2n)-orbit closures in the flag variety. To prove this result, we construct an analogue of Lascoux's inflation on these objects, providing a combinatorial realization of the symplectic transition equations that appear in work of the first author, Marberg, and Pawlowski. We also show that certain marked symplectic bumpless pipe dreams correspond to set-valued reverse plane partitions. This allows us to give a tableau formula for a class of symplectic Grothendieck polynomials and to compute principal specializations of the corresponding symplectic Schubert polynomials, answering a question of Hamaker-Marberg-Pawlowski in the fixed-point-free case.

papers.title: Toward a human-friendly proof of a polynomial bound for the Directed Grid Theorem
papers.abstract: The Directed Grid Theorem of Kawarabayashi and Kreutzer [STOC 2015] states that there is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that every digraph of directed treewidth at least $f(k)$ contains a cylindrical grid of order $k$ as a butterfly minor. Their function is not elementary, and Hatzel, Kreutzer, Garlet Milani, and Muzi [FOCS 2024] improved it to a tower of exponentials of height $22$, by a proof in three stages through paths and cycles of well-linked sets. In this paper we prove each stage with a polynomial bound, so that $f$ can be chosen to be a polynomial of degree $20\,031\,568$. As a consequence, Younger's conjecture, proved by Reed, Robertson, Seymour, and Thomas [Combinatorica, 1996], holds with a polynomial bound: for the polynomial $f$ that we construct, every digraph without $k$ pairwise disjoint cycles has a feedback vertex set of size at most $(k-1)f(k)$. In fact, beyond cycles, we obtain polynomial packing-covering bounds for every strongly connected digraph that is a butterfly minor of a cylindrical grid.

papers.title: Recursive Word Conditioning for Higher-Dimensional Partitions: Exact Enumeration and Complexity
papers.abstract: Let $p_d(n)$ denote the number of $d$-dimensional partitions of weight $n$. We develop an exact enumeration method operating on recursively parsed partition words (which are shown to encode $d$-dimensional partitions), beginning with an elementary interior-part decomposition of ordinary partitions. Conditioning on an interior word block separates the preceding and succeeding nested blocks. For higher-dimensional partitions, transversely re-parsing the preceding words permits the same conditioning operation to be iterated. Recursive containment and joins carry effective floors across the cuts, while a nonnegative excess permits exact truncation and pruning. The resulting procedure is a complete row-conditioning algorithm. For every fixed $d\ge3$, we prove that it computes $p_d(0),\ldots,p_d(N)$ using at most $\exp\!\bigl(O_d(N^{(d-1)/(d+1)}\log(N+2))\bigr)$ arithmetic operations. A diagonal refinement replaces the final row-conditioning stages by coupled interlacing chains of ordinary-partition words and sharpens the bound to $\exp\!\bigl(O_d(N^{(d-1)/(d+1)})\bigr)$. The algorithms count constrained completions through reusable weight-indexed coefficients rather than enumerating finished partitions. Exact computations with these algorithms reach weights 100, 50, 45, 40 and 35 in dimensions 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7, respectively. On a single 2.1\,GHz core the program computes $p_3(0),\ldots,p_3(100)$ in under four hours and each of the tables in dimensions 4--7 in under 30 minutes.

papers.title: Monoid Representation of the Determinants of the Adjacency Matrices of 1-joined Path Graphs
papers.abstract: Following previous work by these authors, this paper explores all labeled path graphs joined by 1 edge where the labeling contains the information on how to join that graph. The algebraic structure that this operation has on the determinant of the adjacency matrix of the graph gives a finite monoid of matrices under matrix multiplication. We completely characterize the monoid using the representation theory discussed in Khovanov et al(2024). Finally, we demonstrate how these results can be used to find general formulas for the determinants of chains of 1-joined labeled paths.

papers.title: The Vinogradov system in finite fields and two-source extractors with arbitrarily small min-entropy rate
papers.abstract: Fix $k\ge2$ and $1/(k+1)<\rho\le1$. Let $q=p^n$, where the prime $p$ is fixed and sufficiently large in terms of $k,\rho$, and $n$ tends to infinity through prime values. We show that for every $A\subseteq\F_q$ with $|A|\ge q^\rho$, the Vinogradov system of degree $k$ in $2s$ variables has at most $|A|^{2s}q^{-k/2-\eta}$ solutions in $A$. Here the integer $s$ and the saving $\eta>0$ depend only on $k,\rho,p$. At $\rho=1/(k+1)$ an example rules out every saving $\eta>0$ in this moment estimate. For $k=2$ the author previously proved the analogous estimate over prime fields. We deduce a power saving for the double sums of $e(xy+(xy)^2+\dots+(xy)^k)$ over any two sets of size at least $q^\rho$, where $e$ is any nontrivial additive character of $\F_q$. Choosing $k$ sufficiently large gives a polynomial two-source extractor with exponentially small error at every fixed positive min-entropy rate. The proof of the moment estimate uses the theorem of Gowers, Green, Manners and Tao on Marton's conjecture and a bound for the intersection of the moment curve with an affine subspace over $\F_p$.

papers.title: Real equiangular lines in dimensions 18-20 and sharp fixed-angle bounds
papers.abstract: In collaboration with OpenAI's GPT-6, we prove that the maximum numbers of real equiangular lines in dimensions 18, 19, and 20 are $N(18)=57$, $N(19)=72$, and $N(20)=90$, respectively. We reduce the upper bounds to paired lattice points in sections of even unimodular lattices of rank twenty-four. Root-system estimates, exact certificates, and Golay-code arguments bound the sections. In the Leech lattice, generalized Hamming weights of a binary evaluation code give sharp bounds attained by nested sections. At prescribed cosine $1/q$, we also show that $N_{1/q}(d)=d+7$ for explicit intervals of consecutive dimensions for each odd $q\ge319$, and $N_{1/q}(d)=d+23$ on such intervals for each odd $q\ge5599$. Regular graphs in repeated Seidel blocks vary the cosine while preserving nullity, and a coherence bound proves optimality. Symmetric conference matrices give a further sharp family at quadratic irrational cosines.

papers.title: On a Problem of Erdős and Graham Related to Restricted Order
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a set of nonnegative integers. We prove that if $A\setminus F$ has a finite order for every finite subset $F\subseteq A$, then $A$ has finite restricted order. This resolves a problem posed by Erd\H{o}s and Graham in 1980. We also establish a local to global principle to characterize restricted asymptotic bases of finite order.

papers.title: Semisimple-Unipotent Decomposition and the Exact Order of a Linear Cellular Automaton over F_2
papers.abstract: We study the linear cellular automaton on the cyclic graph $C_n$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ defined by the local rule $v_i(t+1)=v_{i-1}(t)\oplus v_i(t)\oplus v_{i+1}(t)$ (Wolfram's Rule 150 under periodic boundary conditions). Identifying the configuration space $V_n=\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $R_n = \mathbb{F}_2[x] / \langle x^n - 1 \rangle$, the evolution operator corresponds to multiplication by $G(x)=1+x+x^{n-1}$. We re-derive the invertibility criterion $3\nmid n$, classify periodic and transient behaviour, and prove that Hamming weight is non-monotone for every $n\ge3$. We then factor $x^n-1$ via the Chinese Remainder Theorem and separate semisimple contributions governed by finite-field multiplicative orders from unipotent contributions governed by Frobenius squaring. We determine the exact local unipotent orders and obtain a closed-form global order $r(A)$: $r(A)=2^{m-1}$ for $n=2^m$ with $m\ge2$, while for $n=2^m q$, $q>1$ odd and $3\nmid n$, $r(A)=2^m\operatorname{lcm}(m_2,\ldots,m_r)$. The theory is illustrated by $n=5,7,8,16$ and computationally verified for small dimensions.

papers.title: The smallest vertex triangle in a fixed polygon
papers.abstract: Among the triangles determined by $n$ points in convex position in the unit square, one has area at most $32/n^3$. Equality is possible exactly when $4$ divides $n$, and then the maximizing point set is unique. We prove a fixed-container theorem for a class of convex $s$-gons that includes affinely regular polygons and a one-parameter family of pairwise affinely inequivalent hexagons without a centre of symmetry. If the container has equal ears of area $a$ and the tips of its directed side vectors are in convex position, the sharp bound at $n=sk$ is $a/k^3$. Its equality conditions determine every side vector of the maximizing polygon. The proof uses the area enclosed by the normalized side directions. We compare the result with the area-normalized smallest-ear theorem of Gronchi and Longinetti and give consequences for unrestricted Heilbronn configurations with 13 and 15 points.

papers.title: The regular polygon maximizes the first positive Steklov eigenvalue among simple polygons at fixed area
papers.abstract: For $N\ge5$ and every simple planar polygon $P$ with at most $N$ sides, $\sqrt{|P|}\,\sigma_1(P)\le\sqrt{|R_N|}\,\sigma_1(R_N)$, where $\sigma_1$ is the first positive Steklov eigenvalue and $R_N$ is a regular $N$-gon. Equality holds precisely for polygons similar to $R_N$. This answers Oudet's fixed-area open problem \cite{AIM} for all $N\ge5$.

papers.title: From random intersection to spatial graphs: a unified asymptotic framework
papers.abstract: Random intersection graphs and spatial random graphs provide different mechanisms for generating edges and clustering. We investigate their interplay through geometric random intersection graphs, where vertices are adjacent whenever they share a spatially located group. First, a Poisson decomposition by attachment sets yields exact subgraph probabilities and laws of large numbers for connected subgraph densities. It distinguishes triangles supported by a common group from those requiring three distinct groups. Second, explicit representations of global and average local clustering reveal their different dependence on model parameters and the role of shared groups in edge correlations. Finally, by varying the strength and spatial range of group memberships, we establish convergence to random connection, random geometric, random intersection, Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi, and complete graphs. We characterize the corresponding clustering limits and show that clustering need not converge to that of the limiting graph, highlighting the distinction between spatially local convergence and global graph statistics.

papers.title: Fast Algorithms for Permanents of Permutationally-Dominant Matrices
papers.abstract: We establish a fast algorithm for approximating the permanent of permutationally-dominant matrices. In particular, we obtain a fully polynomial randomised approximation scheme whose runtime is quadratic in both the dimension of the matrix and the inverse of the approximation error. Our approach is based on a polymer model representation of the permanent and importance sampling of the logarithm of its partition function via the theory of heaps of pieces of Viennot.

papers.title: On the Cluster Duration Distribution of the Markovian Hawkes Process
papers.abstract: The duration of a Hawkes process cluster, meaning the time from first point to last point in an entirely endogenously generated progeny stream, has been stubbornly resistant to analysis; even the mean has not been known in closed form. Recently, uniformly random parking functions have been found to be hidden spines of these history-driven clusters, offering a probabilistic combinatorial structure within self-excitement that has opened new avenues for analysis. Here, we leverage and refine this decomposition to provide a closed-form expression for the mean cluster duration in the case of an exponential excitation kernel. Specifically, we reduce from uniformly random parking functions to non-uniform preference counts. This change of probabilistic combinatorial structure in the decomposition leads us to both a Borel-based identity and an explicit integral-based expression for the mean duration.

papers.title: A proof of the Nevo-Peeva conjecture: Exact regularity and linear powers of gap-free edge ideals
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with at least one edge, and let $I(G)$ be its edge ideal over a field $K$. We prove that if $G$ is gap-free, then $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)^q=\max\{2q,\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)+q-1\}$ for all $q\geq 1$. This answers both open problems of Nevo and Peeva on ordinary powers: $I(G)^q$ has a linear resolution exactly when $q\geq \mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-1$, and their proposed regularity recurrence holds with equality. As consequences, the upper bound $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)^q\leq 2q+\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-2$ conjectured by Alilooee, Banerjee, Beyarslan, H\`a, Jayanthan and Selvaraja holds for gap-free graphs; every power $I(G)^q$ with $q\geq 2$ has a linear resolution when $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)=3$; and the stabilization index equals $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-1$, which is unbounded on this class. The proof rests on a combinatorial result of independent interest: a parity-sensitive homology vanishing theorem for a filtration of the independence complex by a weighted Hall defect. An internalization lemma and sublevel complexes of submodular functions control the local terms, and Hall's theorem together with an implication-digraph argument classifies the zero level. A capacitated form of the Tutte-Berge formula and Takayama's formula identify the filtration with the degree complexes of ordinary powers. The algebraic statements hold over every field, and the topological vanishing holds with arbitrary abelian coefficients.

papers.title: Extension complexity is not additive under Cartesian products
papers.abstract: We prove that the linear extension complexity of a Cartesian product of polytopes can be strictly smaller than the sum of the extension complexities of its factors. This disproves Conjecture 1.2 of Grande, Padrol and Sanyal. We construct a rational 24-dimensional polytope $P$ with 50 facets and 150 vertices such that $P$ has extension complexity 40 and $P \times P$ has extension complexity exactly 79. We also prove that the saving can be arbitrarily large, even in a Cartesian square: for every $t$ there is a rational polytope $R_t$ whose square needs at least $t$ fewer inequalities than two separate copies of $R_t$. For two different factors, we construct a family whose product saves at least $\lceil 5n/27 \rceil$ inequalities while the two separate complexities sum to $O(n)$, so that the saving is a constant fraction of the total. The proofs rest on a transfer theorem: wedging over the omitted facets of a polytope turns a gap between the nonnegative ranks of partial slack matrices into a gap between extension complexities. The unbounded squares come from intersecting families of sets on successively larger alphabets. In the square the two copies of each coordinate share generators, while a counting lemma determines the exact cost of a single factor.

papers.title: Explicit covers and rigid obstructions for simplicial complexity: from spheres to surfaces
papers.abstract: The strict simplicial complexity $SC_{\rm strict}(K)$, Gonz\'alez's simplicial complexity at subdivision level zero, is one less than the least number of contiguity domains covering the ordered product $K\times K$. We bound it from both sides. For upper bounds, every product of two vertex stars is a domain, which gives $SC_{\rm strict}(K)\le\rho(K)-1$ for an exactly computable set-cover number $\rho(K)$; the bound is sharp on every even-dimensional simplex boundary. A GPU annealer that evolves whole systems of contiguity chains finds three-domain covers of $\partial\Delta^3,\dots,\partial\Delta^7$ and of the cube boundary. Seeded by star covers, it descends from $24$ to $5$ domains on the icosahedron boundary, and an exact SAT completion of its stalled state gives $SC_{\rm strict}\le3$ there. For lower bounds, a subcomplex of $K\times K$ is rigid if its two projections are joined by no contiguity chain of any length; $k$ domains can cover $K\times K$ only if $k$ classes of facets avoid every rigid subcomplex, a finite SAT problem. Rigid subcomplexes arise from hollow triangles over essential empty triangles and, on complexes without dominated vertices, from the graph of every order-preserving simplicial self-map other than the identity. The resultingchain-length-free bounds give $SC_{\rm strict}(\partial\Delta^{n+1})=2>1=TC(S^n)$ for $n=3,5,7,9$, $SC_{\rm strict}=2>1$ for the five-vertex M\"obius band, $SC_{\rm strict}\ge3>2$ for the seven-vertex torus, and $4\le SC_{\rm strict}\le5$ and $4\le SC_{\rm strict}\le6$ for two triangulations of $\mathbb{RP}^2$. They also sort the annealer's stalls: on these two triangulations of $\mathbb{RP}^2$, the Klein bottle and $\partial\Delta^4$, almost every uncovered facet closes a rigid subcomplex in every domain, while the icosahedron stall was a search failure.

papers.title: PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models
papers.abstract: There are several approaches to AI-driven mathematical discovery. One of these involves the use of large language models (LLMs) to resolve well-specified conjectures via text-based reasoning, while another uses narrow models and interpretability for more open-ended, human-in-the-loop exploration using object-based mathematical data. The latter is limited in its ability to move beyond simple empirical pattern detection while the former is not well-designed for direct, open-ended exploration of large mathematical datasets. In this paper we introduce PatternMiner, a system that combines these two paradigms. In PatternMiner, an LLM agent generates mathematical datasets based on an initial broad question, trains narrow machine learning models on them, uses interpretability techniques to extract patterns from these trained models, and uses these patterns to formulate conjectures. Once an initial conjecture has been formulated, PatternMiner instructs the agent to search for counterexamples using calls to mathematical software. If a set of counterexamples can be found, these are used as feedback for conjecture refinement or another round of training and interpretability. The conjecture progressively evolves through this iterative sequence with the agent allowed to try to prove it at any point. We describe the results of applying PatternMiner to five well-known positivity problems in algebraic combinatorics. PatternMiner proves several new theorems related to Schubert positivity and projection, a character-row evaluation formula, a restricted version of the Kazhdan--Lusztig combinatorial invariance conjecture, and Schur positivity for a family of immanant coefficients. We end by analyzing the most common routes to conjecture generation that are used by PatternMiner in our case studies as well as documenting the most common failure modes.

papers.title: Schwinger-Dyson recursion, Gröbner elimination and graph combinatorics
papers.abstract: Schwinger-Dyson equations are a cornerstone of quantum field theory (QFT). Derived using integration by parts, they capture relations between correlators of different orders, forming an open, infinite-dimensional system. In zero-dimensional QFTs with polynomial actions, which is just a physical interpretation for multivariate Gaussian integrals with polynomial insertions, conventional Gr\"obner elimination can be used to express all higher-order correlators (moments) in terms of a fixed basis set. One consequence is a closed finite-dimensional system of differential equations for the coupling dependence of these `master' correlators. An important application of zero-dimensional QFTs is in counting discrete geometric structures (as in simplicial approaches to quantum gravity). For the problem of counting labelled regular graphs, applying this Schwinger-Dyson closure results in a computational breakthrough relative to the existing state-of-the-art: for 9- and 10-regular graphs on $n$ vertices, a finite-depth, finite-width recursive formulation is obtained, making it possible to compute the total graph counts in $O(n)$ arithmetic operations.

papers.title: Equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of orthogonal groups
papers.abstract: We construct explicit symmetric-function realizations of the torus-equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of types B and D. More precisely, we realize the extended $K$-theoretic Peterson algebras as subalgebras of a completed ring of equivariant symmetric functions and identify their Schubert classes in terms of symmetric functions. We introduce two new families of equivariant symmetric functions for each of types B and D and prove that these functions represent the classes of the structure sheaves of Schubert varieties and the ideal sheaves of their boundaries, respectively. We establish several fundamental properties of these functions, including translation factorization formulas and explicit expressions for the classes indexed by small affine Grassmannian elements. In type D, we further describe the action of the affine Dynkin diagram automorphism interchanging the two spin nodes and show how it intertwines the Schubert bases with a nontrivial transformation of the equivariant parameters.

papers.title: A note on characterization of S4 x C2^n
papers.abstract: For every non-negative integer n, we characterize S4 x C2^n by its poset of isomorphic classes of subgroups. This provides an infinite family of counterexamples to the conjectures posed by Tarnauceanu in [8] and [9].

papers.title: Splitting of multiplicity spaces into symmetric and alternating parts
On the Density of Repeated Entries in Pascal's Triangle
papers.abstract: Let $N(a)$ denote the number of occurrences of the integer $a>1$ in Pascal's triangle, and set ${\mathcal E}_H=\{a\geq3:N(a)>2H\}$, $A_H(x)=|{\mathcal E}_H\cap[1,x]|.$ For every fixed $K\geq2$ we prove the expansion $A_1(x)=\sum_{k=2}^{K}(k!x)^{1/k}+O_K\!\left(x^{1/(K+1)}\right).$ Consequently, the Dirichlet series ${D}_1(s)=\sum_{a\in{\mathcal E}_1}a^{-s}$ extends meromorphically to $\Re s>0$, with simple poles precisely at $s=1/k$, $k\geq2$, of residue $(k!)^{1/k}/k$. For every $H\geq2$, $x\ge 3$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove $A_H(x)\le A_2(x)\leq\exp\left(\frac{2\log x}{(\log\log x)^{1/4}}\right)\ll_{\varepsilon} x^{\varepsilon}.$ Hence $D_H(s)=\sum_{a\in{\mathcal E}_H}a^{-s}$ is holomorphic for $\Re s>0$ when $H\geq2$, and $\lambda({\mathcal E}_1)=1/2, \lambda({\mathcal E}_H)=0\quad(H\geq2).$ Here, for a set $S\subseteq {\mathbb N}$, its exponent of convergence is $\lambda(S)=\inf\left\{\sigma>0: \sum_{n\in S}n^{-\sigma}<\infty\right\}.$ We also determine the logarithmic-order counting law for the classical Lind--Singmaster family of coefficients of multiplicity at least six.

papers.title: Full Structure Recovery of Linearized Reed-Solomon Codes
papers.abstract: Linearized Reed-Solomon codes (LRS) are optimal sum-rank-metric codes that generalize both Reed-Solomon and Gabidulin codes, and benefit from excellent decoding capabilities, making them potentially interesting candidates for post-quantum code-based cryptography. Previous works have investigated the underlying geometric structure of LRS codes, identifying geometric invariants that distinguish them from random codes. Other works have proposed approaches to recovering the LRS structure from an arbitrary generator matrix, together with additional data. However, both the distinguishers and the recovery techniques proposed so far are either not fully general, or have a prohibitive computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a polynomial-time procedure for the full structure recovery of LRS codes from the sole knowledge of an arbitrary generator matrix. Our results show that, like their Hamming and rank metric counterparts, LRS codes cannot be used as they are for McEliece-like encryption. Our approach combines Overbeck-type attacks with suitable matrix manipulations and shortening techniques to recover the evaluation parameters across different ranges of code dimensions.
